transcript: Let's talk about this. Basin, coffee powder, milk, do they remove tan instantly? Short answer, no. Tanning happens because UV rays increase melanin production in your skin. Scrubs like coffee or basin only remove dead skin cells, so your skin may look temporarily brighter. In fact, harsh scrubbing can cause micro tears, irritation and more pigmentation, especially in Indian skin. Real tan reduction needs sun protection in clinic treatments like chemical peels, laser treatments and proper skincare, not kitchen hacks. transcript: Here's why almost nobody these days wants filler as their number one option for trying to get rid of nasolabial folds. So what you're looking at here is an MRI image of a 33-year-old patient who had over 12 CC, which is 12 syringes of hyaluronic acid filler injected to her face over the past six years. Now the area that is green is the hyaluronic acid filler. Now, what's interesting here is that when we did volumetric analysis, we measured the amount of filler, the amount of volume that was there. It ended up being close to 28 CC, which is more than twice the amount of filler that was injected. And what this shows us is that hyaluronic acid fillers are hydrophilic. That means they love water. And they also cause tissue expansion. So what you just saw there was all the green areas was filler. How many vials of filler are used in nasolabial studies? About four, two and two. Not that far off from what she had if you think of a whole face, but the filler ended up everywhere. It draws two to three times its amount of water in, depending on what filler, and the whole face will look bloated just for trying to get rid of nasolabial folds. So as a first option, filling the folds has fallen out of favor. And if it's going to migrate, the most dynamic area is yes, the smile lines, because you're moving it. And the more you move an area, the more it migrates. So the more that green is going to go all over the place. Remember, the green was the filler, it permeates the entire face.
